request.system:
You check whether short claims are faithful to the source texts they cite.

The claims form one answer and are read together: a condition or exception stated in another claim does not need to be repeated, and a claim that summarises part of a text is faithful if that part is accurate. Mark a claim unfaithful only when it asserts something the cited texts contradict or do not support.

For each claim, answer: does the claim follow from the cited texts alone, without adding, narrowing, or changing anything they say? A claim that paraphrases or restates accurately is faithful — identical wording is not required. A claim that introduces a number, condition, or conclusion the texts do not support is not. Each cited text is labelled with its reference (e.g. "3.A.6") and title; a claim may use that label. Judge only the substance of the claim against its texts; ignore whether it answers any particular question and ignore framing about what a text is or is not about. Give a one-sentence reason.
request.user:
Claim 0: Under 3.A.4, new portfolios must be included in a composite no later than the beginning of the second full calendar month after the portfolio comes under management.
  Cited texts:
    [prov:composite-inclusion-timing@E2021] 3.A.4 Timing of new portfolio inclusion: New portfolios must be included in a composite on a timely and consistent basis, and no later than the beginning of the second full calendar month after the portfolio comes under management, unless the composite-specific policy documented by the firm specifies an earlier date.

Claim 1: Inclusion must also be on a timely and consistent basis (3.A.4).
  Cited texts:
    [prov:composite-inclusion-timing@E2021] 3.A.4 Timing of new portfolio inclusion: New portfolios must be included in a composite on a timely and consistent basis, and no later than the beginning of the second full calendar month after the portfolio comes under management, unless the composite-specific policy documented by the firm specifies an earlier date.

Claim 2: If the firm's documented composite-specific policy specifies an earlier date, that earlier date governs (3.A.4).
  Cited texts:
    [prov:composite-inclusion-timing@E2021] 3.A.4 Timing of new portfolio inclusion: New portfolios must be included in a composite on a timely and consistent basis, and no later than the beginning of the second full calendar month after the portfolio comes under management, unless the composite-specific policy documented by the firm specifies an earlier date.

Claim 3: A composite is an aggregation of one or more portfolios managed according to a similar investment mandate, objective, or strategy (1.D.1).
  Cited texts:
    [def:composite@E2021] 1.D.1 Composite: A composite is an aggregation of one or more portfolios managed according to a similar investment mandate, objective, or strategy.

verdicts.reason: Matches the main rule in 3.A.4; the earlier-date exception is stated in another claim and the claims are read together.
3.A.4 requires inclusion on a timely and consistent basis.
The text says the second-full-month limit applies unless the documented composite-specific policy specifies an earlier date, so the earlier date governs.
This restates the 1.D.1 definition of a composite accurately.
